m102.text: Basil tests which makes a stronger electromagnet, an iron nail or a steel nail. He coils twenty-five turns round the iron nail, but only eight turns round the steel nail. Is his test fair?

m201b.text: Our mini crane needs the strongest hook. So I am testing an iron nail and a steel nail!

m204.text: A little woodlouse is hiding in this video. Can you spot it?

m205p.text: Woodlice love dark, damp corners. Look low!

m206.text: You against the Buddies! Lock in first with your fingers. One finger for every point.

m304m.text: How to spot an unfair test.

h501.text: Are you ready? Three! Two! One! Go!

m401.text: Round one! Is Basil's test fair? One, yes. Two, no. Show me your fingers!

m403b.text: One! It's my test, and my iron nail picked up the most clips. Iron wins!

m404p.text: Two. The iron nail has many more turns of wire. Maybe the turns did it.

m405m.text: Two. Basil changed the nail, and he changed the turns too.

m501.text: Be a steel paper clip! Shrink down. Quietly.

m502.text: You are a steel paper clip, lying in a tray. Above you hangs Basil's iron nail, wrapped in many, many turns of wire.

m503.text: It pulls you up, hard! You cling to its tip with lots of other clips. Over there, the steel nail has only a few turns. Its pull is weak.

m504.text: But you wonder. Was it the iron that pulled you? Or all those turns? You cannot tell!

m601.text: The answer is two: Basil's test is not fair! Did you show two fingers? Put one finger up!

m602p.text: A variable is a thing that can change in a test, such as the kind of nail, or the number of turns!

m701b.text: But my iron nail picked up the most clips. Why is that not fair?

m702.text: Look closer. Basil changed two things. The kind of nail is different. And the number of turns is different too.

m703.text: The iron nail attracts more clips. Was it because of the iron? Or because of the twenty-five turns? We cannot be sure.

m704s.text: If the experiment is not fair, we will not be sure which variable can explain the results.

m705m.text: A fair test is a test where we change only one thing, and keep all the other things the same, such as changing only the kind of nail!

m707.text: To conduct a fair test, scientists need to ensure that only one thing, called a variable, is changed. The other variables are kept the same.

m801m.text: Pip, my magnet picked up more pins than yours! So my magnet is the stronger one!

m802.text: Something is not right. If you can spot it, cross your arms. Hold on!

m804b.text: Momo held her magnet close to the pins, and Pip held his far away. The distance changed too! Hold them at the same height, over the same pins.

m805p.text: Now only the magnet is different. That is fair!

m901b.text: Okay! How do I make my iron and steel test fair?

m902.text: Look closer. Give both nails twenty turns of wire. Use the same kind of battery, the same wire, and the same steel clips.

m903.text: Dip both tips the same way. Now only one thing is different: the kind of nail. If one nail attracts more clips, we know the nail did it!

m904b.text: An experiment is a test that we plan and do to answer a question, such as: which nail makes a stronger electromagnet?

m906.text: When scientists plan and conduct an experiment, they answer a question or test a prediction.

m1001.text: Show me your score hand! Two fingers? You beat the Buddies. High five!

m1002.text: Did you spot the woodlouse? It was under the cupboard door!

m1003b.text: Here is a fun fact! A woodlouse is a cousin of crabs and prawns! And in a fair test, with a damp side and a dry side, woodlice crawl to the damp side!

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?

m1101m.text: My turn! I will test if more batteries make our electromagnet stronger!

m1102.text: Will Momo's plan be fair? Find out in Part Two!
